title: Applied AI for Supervisory Staff
summary: An eight-module hands-on programme helping supervisory staff use generative AI and analytics tools safely and productively in everyday supervisory work.
intro: This training programme equips supervisory staff to use generative AI and analytics tools safely and productively in day-to-day work, from reviewing firm documents and returns to drafting, data analysis and verifying outputs.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors the practical skills and confidence to use the authority's approved AI tools on real supervisory tasks, within its AI policy and confidentiality rules. Participants leave able to write effective prompts, speed up document review, drafting and analysis, and check AI outputs to the evidential standard supervisory work demands.
sections.What It Covers: Generative AI essentials, the authority's AI policy and confidentiality, prompting for supervisory tasks, reviewing firm documents and returns, drafting correspondence and reports, data analysis, verification and professional judgement, and building AI into supervisory workflows.
Intended Audience: Supervisors, inspectors, analysts and authorisation staff at all levels of seniority
Policy, enforcement and financial crime staff who review documents, data and correspondence
Team leaders responsible for embedding AI tools safely in their teams' work
Learning Objectives: Explain how generative AI tools work, what they do well and where they fail
Apply the authority's AI policy, including data classification and confidentiality rules
Write structured prompts that produce reliable outputs for supervisory tasks
Use AI to review firm documents and returns, draft correspondence and analyse data
Verify AI outputs and retain professional judgement and accountability for every decision
Design repeatable AI-assisted workflows and share good practice across the team
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day workshops. Each module is hands-on, built around live exercises on realistic supervisory tasks using the authority's approved tools, and modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's AI policy and systems.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Everyday familiarity with office software is helpful. No prior experience of AI tools or data analysis is required.
Core Reading: FSB, The Use of Supervisory and Regulatory Technology by Authorities and Regulated Institutions (2020)
BIS Financial Stability Institute, Innovative Technology in Financial Supervision (Suptech): The Experience of Early Users (FSI Insights No 9, 2018)
NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (2023)

modules.title: Generative AI Essentials for Supervisory Work
modules.summary: A practical introduction to how generative AI and large language models work, what they can and cannot do, and where they add value in supervisory work.
objectives: Explain in plain terms how large language models generate text
Identify strengths and limits, including hallucination and outdated knowledge
Recognise the supervisory tasks where AI tools add most value
syllabus: How large language models work: training, prompts and probabilistic output
Chat assistants, document tools, analytics tools and AI built into office software
Typical failure modes: hallucination, omission, overconfidence and bias
Mapping the supervisory day: where AI helps and where it should not be used

modules.title: Using AI Safely: Policy, Confidentiality and Data
modules.summary: The rules that govern AI use in the authority, covering approved tools, data classification, confidential supervisory information, records and accountability, so staff can use AI with confidence.
objectives: Apply the authority's AI policy and approved-tool list to everyday tasks
Classify information correctly before it is shared with an AI tool
Identify confidentiality, data protection and record-keeping obligations
syllabus: The authority's AI policy: [approved tools, permitted uses and prohibited uses]
Confidential supervisory information, personal data and firm data
Records, audit trails and disclosure of AI assistance
Scenarios: safe, unsafe and grey-area uses

modules.title: Prompting for Supervisory Tasks
modules.summary: How to write clear, structured prompts that give AI tools the role, context, task and output format they need, and how to refine prompts until results are dependable.
objectives: Structure prompts using role, context, task, constraints and format
Refine outputs through iteration, examples and follow-up questions
Build a reusable prompt library for common supervisory tasks
syllabus: Anatomy of a good prompt and common prompting mistakes
Grounding the tool in source documents rather than its general knowledge
Step-by-step reasoning, checklists and structured outputs
Exercise: building team prompt templates

modules.title: Reviewing Firm Documents and Returns
modules.summary: Using AI to read, summarise and compare firm submissions, policies, board packs and regulatory returns more quickly, while keeping control of what matters to the supervisory judgement.
objectives: Summarise long firm documents and board packs accurately
Compare firm policies against requirements and previous submissions
Extract key data and identify anomalies in firm returns
syllabus: Summarising board minutes, risk reports and business plans
Gap analysis of policies against rules, guidance and good practice
Comparing submissions over time and across peer firms
Exercise: preparing for a firm meeting with AI-assisted review

modules.title: Drafting with AI: Letters, Reports and Briefings
modules.summary: How to use AI to draft and improve supervisory letters, inspection reports, internal briefings and meeting notes in the authority's style, while keeping findings accurate and defensible.
objectives: Draft supervisory correspondence and reports from structured notes
Edit drafts for clarity, tone and the authority's house style
Ensure every finding in an AI-assisted draft is supported by evidence
syllabus: From notes to first draft: findings letters and inspection reports
Briefing papers and summaries for senior management and committees
Plain language, tone and consistency with the authority's style
Exercise: drafting and reviewing a findings letter

modules.title: Data Analysis with AI Tools
modules.summary: Using AI-enabled analytics to explore, clean, analyse and visualise supervisory data, from firm returns to complaints and market data, without needing to be a data specialist.
objectives: Use AI tools to clean, structure and explore supervisory datasets
Generate and check analysis, formulas and charts
Interpret results and recognise misleading or unreliable analysis
syllabus: Asking questions of spreadsheets and regulatory return data
Trend, peer and outlier analysis for risk identification
AI-generated formulas, queries and code: checking before trusting
Exercise: identifying outlier firms from return data

modules.title: Verification, Bias and Professional Judgement
modules.summary: How to check AI outputs to the standard supervisory work requires, recognise bias and error, and keep accountability for conclusions and decisions with the supervisor, not the tool.
objectives: Apply structured techniques to verify AI outputs against sources
Recognise bias, omission and automation bias in AI-assisted work
Maintain accountability and an evidential trail for supervisory decisions
syllabus: Source checking, citation testing and cross-checking with a second method
Automation bias and the temptation to over-rely on fluent output
When AI must not be used: decisions, sanctions and sensitive judgements
Exercise: finding the errors in an AI-generated analysis

modules.title: Building AI into Supervisory Workflows
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by redesigning everyday supervisory tasks around AI, measuring the benefit, sharing good practice and agreeing each participant's practical action plan.
objectives: Redesign recurring supervisory tasks as AI-assisted workflows
Measure time saved, quality and risk in AI-assisted work
Produce a personal and team plan for productive, safe AI use
syllabus: Mapping recurring tasks and choosing the right tool for each step
Reusable templates, prompt libraries and team guidance
Feedback to the authority's AI governance and SupTech teams
Workshop: personal and team AI action plans

related.title: Agentic Finance for Supervisors
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to understand and supervise AI agents that transact and make financial decisions, from agent identity to payments and liability.

related.title: AI Governance for Supervisors
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess firms' AI governance, model and fairness risk, and to shape the authority's approach to AI supervision.

related.title: Financial Crime Supervision in the Age of AI
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess financial crime controls and firms' use of AI in monitoring, screening, fraud and surveillance.

related.title: FinTech Business Models: Understanding and Supervising Innovation
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and firm compliance teams to understand how FinTech business models make money, grow and fail, and to assess their risks.

related.title: SupTech, Data and Supervisory Analytics
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and leaders to govern supervisory data, interrogate returns, use analytics to surface risk and build the authority's SupTech capability.

related.title: The EU AI Act and Financial Services (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on the EU AI Act for supervisors and financial firms: risk classification, high-risk credit and insurance uses, provider and deployer duties, supervision and compliance programmes.
